title: Trump Backs Hegseth as GOP Lawmaker Moves to Impeach Defense Chief Over Iran War
snippet: President Donald Trump is standing behind Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth as Rep. Thomas Massie reintroduced articles of impeachment following severe Republican midterm losses linked to the ongoing war in Iran.
content:
WASHINGTON — President Donald Trump signaled unwavering support for Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth on Monday, rejecting a freshly reintroduced impeachment effort by a Republican lawmaker as Congress returned to Capitol Hill following a disastrous midterm election for the GOP.

Kentucky Rep. Thomas Massie reintroduced articles of impeachment accusing the Pentagon chief of committing "high crimes and misdemeanors." Massie alleged that Hegseth breached the War Powers Resolution by directing military actions abroad, specifically in Iran, without explicit congressional authorization or a formal declaration of war.

Impeachment Push Adds Pressure in Lame-Duck Session

Speaking on the House floor, Massie argued that Hegseth acted in a manner "grossly incompatible with his duties and the rule of law" and urged his removal from office. Massie, who lost his own primary battle earlier this year, had previously pushed for Hegseth’s impeachment in September before House Speaker Mike Johnson postponed the vote.

Because the resolution only requires a simple majority to pass the House, a handful of Republican defections combined with a unified Democratic block could force an impeachment vote through the chamber before the end of the term.

Trump, however, dismissed the effort and slammed Massie's intentions. "Yeah, I'll stand by him," Trump told reporters, adding that he believes Massie "has a lot of hatred in his heart" while maintaining that Hegseth is doing a "very good job."

GOP Finger-Pointing Follows Midterm Blowout

The escalation against Hegseth comes as Republicans grapple with losing control of both the House and Senate in last week's midterm elections. Several top figures within the party have directly linked the electoral defeats to the soaring economic costs and military strain associated with the U.S.-led war in Iran.

Vice President JD Vance recently acknowledged on social media that the conflict was the primary driver behind the party's loss. Other key Republicans, including North Carolina Sen. Thom Tillis, have openly called for Hegseth’s dismissal, citing poor administrative management and unnecessary distractions.

Pentagon Prepares Defense

Despite mounting pressure from both sides of the aisle and incoming Democratic committee leadership promising swift oversight investigations next year, Hegseth has remained defiant.

In a recent message addressed to the public, Hegseth labeled the move a "sham impeachment" backed by political adversaries. The Defense Secretary expressed confidence that the effort would collapse and indicated he would address the situation further during a scheduled Pentagon press briefing on Tuesday.
